Not every dog can do this, and not every trainer can or should. With the owners' permission, I used Bishop to help communicate a lesson to Ryder. Dogs naturally understand other dogs better than they understand us. The goal wasn't to make Ryder love every dog she sees-it was to teach her that she doesn't need to react to every dog she sees. Before training, a simple neighborhood walk was nearly impossible. Seeing another dog meant lunging, pulling, and trying to start conflict. Through obedience work and carefully controlled sessions with Bishop, Ryder learned a valuable lesson: not every dog is a threat, and not every situation requires a reaction. Also notice how Bishop's corrections increase in intensity throughout the video. He starts with the minimum amount of pressure necessary and only escalates when Ryder chooses not to listen. That's how dogs naturally communicate with one another. Will I tell these owners to take her to a dog park and expect her to be everyone's best friend? Absolutely not. But can we give her a better quality of life by helping her calmly walk past another dog across the street? Absolutely. Not every dog needs this type of training, but some dogs can benefit tremendously from it. Japan's most famous Katsudon🍚  If you’ve never had this, you are missing out on one of Japan’s greatest masterpieces. It’s a crispy, golden pork cutlet (Tonkatsu) simmered in a sweet and savory dashi broth with tender onions and silky, marbled eggs—all piled high on a steaming bowl of rice. It’s crunchy, juicy, sweet, savory, and pure perfection in every single bite! 🛒 The Ingredients The Crunch: Pork loin chop breaded in crispy Japanese Panko. The Umami Broth: Dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, and a pinch of sugar. The Topping: Thinly sliced yellow onions and lightly beaten eggs. The Base: Steamed Japanese short-grain rice. 🍳 How It’s Made (The Process) Fry: Season and coat the pork in flour, egg, and panko. Deep fry until golden brown and slice it up. Simmer: Cook the onions in the savory dashi broth until tender. Assemble: Lay the crispy katsu right on top of the onions, pour the swirled eggs around it, and cover until softly set. Slide: Slide the whole glorious thing over a hot bed of rice and garnish with green onions! #japanesefood #japan #katsudon#tonkatsu #donburi#cooking #ricebowl #cookingtiktok #asmrfood #food #Foodie #wokkings #fypシ #viral

Not because she’s a “bad dog”… But because she’s been making decisions for a long time without clear direction. No real structure. No consistent boundaries. No clear communication or expectations. And when you let “dogs be dogs” they do just that.  This is the part people struggle with.. You can love your dog deeply and still be missing the leadership they actually need.
